criteria.rationale: Examined the exit gate (roadmap :74-78) against the code and the fourth measurement run: field-by-field handshake and per-request identity (runtime.go:426,449-455), peer credentials before read (:404-408), restart inherits nothing (T2), standalone fallback (T6), memo keyed by commit/shallow/config with no watcher, no rerun of possibly-run commands, short-query QoS and deterministic output under one and two heavy jobs (T3,T5,T7) with RAM/CPU/latency per scenario. CPU quota and per-command limits are not delivered and are disclosed in ADR :299-304; concluded the gate has falsifiable evidence.

The ADR amendment of 2026-11-10 composes the three slices (endpoint/handshake, hosted checks with resident memo, admission lanes); the hosted handler uses the server's identity check, the lanes and the memo without contradiction; the sealed integration evidence of all three member specs passes.
All three ordered member specs show status: done and have no unchecked task (searched ^- \[ \]); the last commit carries the three member specs.
Examined the sealed cumulative module validation: build, unit and the full integration/reachability set for pose-mcp all pass. Not re-run here because the shell was denied.

Cross-spec departures (no watcher, no CPU quota or per-command limits, Windows standalone, B33 views not reused) are disposed in the ADR's final amendment; the remaining findings N4 and N5 are low and carry follow-ups with owner and date.

findings.action: Compare the concurrent heavy run's output and via with the standalone run before T5 passes, as S6 does.
findings.rationale: The heavy check run alongside the short queries discards its output and via, yet the T5 verdict (:378) claims every hosted run printed the standalone output; lane metrics corroborate it ran hosted, but its output is never compared.

findings.action: Increment busy after the connection leaves inflight (or count the deadline handoff atomically), and make the stop-count test strict again.
findings.rationale: At a deadline busy is incremented before the handler returns, while the connection stays in inflight until the reply is written and closed (runtime.go:369); in that window one command counts twice, so status InFlight can read one too high and a stop overcounts drained.
